resale_co.name: Certificate of Construction Records Clearance (CRC)
resale_co.issued_by: Borough of Far Hills Construction / Code Enforcement Office
resale_co.lead_time: Fee depends on business days before closing or change of occupancy: more than 10 business days for the lowest fee.
requirements: Records review before the sale of any residential structure (Ordinance 2020-14)
Application lists closing date (required), year built, swimming pool and pool fence, finished basement, and any second kitchen, basement, pool house or similar
Office checks for open construction permits, open zoning permits, certificates of occupancy/approvals issued, and zoning approval
The CRC may be approved, approved with conditions, or denied

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Construction Records Clearance Application (closing date required) and submit it with the fee to the Code Enforcement Office, Borough Hall, 6 Prospect Street, Far Hills, or contact Code Enforcement Officer Stephen Mahoney (smahoney@farhillsnj.org, 908.234.0611 ext. 26). The certificate is mailed or held for pickup. The smoke/CO certificate is a separate application to the Fire Official.

evidence.quote: There are two requirements for selling a home in the Borough of Far Hills.
A CRC shall be required prior to the sale of any residential or commercial structure and prior to the rental of any tenant space in a commercial structure within the Borough per
PLEASE SUBMIT COMPLETED APPLICATION WITH PAYMENT TO THE CODE ENFORCEMENT OFFICE
As no building or structure shall be occupied in whole or in part prior to the issuance of a certificate of construction records clearance (CRC).

resale_co.notes: Far Hills does not do a resale CO inspection; instead a Construction Records Clearance (CRC) certificate is required before the sale of any residential structure (Ordinance 2020-14). It is a records check for open construction and zoning permits and issued COs/approvals. The ordinance PDF (2020-14 - Authorizing Construction Records Clearance.pdf, September 2020) is a scanned image with no searchable text, so it was not quoted. The CRC application form says fees are subject to change under N.J.A.C. 5:70-2.9(d). The Code Enforcement Officer's email is a mailto link on the Sell My Home page. A landlord registration program exists for rentals; it is not a resale requirement.

requirements: Smoke alarms on each level and within 10 feet of each separate sleeping area; basement alarms near the stairway to the floor above; listed to UL 217 (combination smoke/CO allowed)
Ten-year sealed battery alarms where none exist or when replacing battery units; original AC-powered alarms may not be replaced with battery alarms
Replace smoke alarms older than 10 years

Age-based rules: before 1977 battery alarms on each level and near bedrooms; 1977 to 8-5-1984 AC alarms outside sleeping areas and basement plus battery on first floor; 8-6-1984 to 4-30-1993 interconnected AC alarms on each level; 5-1-1993 on, interconnected AC alarms in each bedroom and on each level with battery backup
Homes with a monitored NFPA 72 system instead of AC smoke alarms need an inspection and certificate of compliance from a certified alarm contractor or electrician
Carbon monoxide alarms (UL 2034) within 10 feet of each separate sleeping area; replace when 5 to 7 years old per manufacturer
Secondary power source label (such as CAUTION: MULTIPLE SOURCES OF POWER, not handwritten) within 18 inches of the main electrical panel and electric meter; the office can supply labels

authorities.how_to_apply: Fill out the Smoke Detector/Carbon Monoxide Application (check SALE, give the closing date and note any central alarm or secondary power) and submit it with a check payable to Borough of Far Hills to the Fire Official, Steven Dill (sdill@farhillsnj.org, 908.234.0611 ext. 29), Borough Hall, 6 Prospect Street. The fee must accompany the application. A failed inspection can mean added re-inspection fees.

fire_cert.notes: The Borough is its own fire code enforcing agency (municipal). The April 2025 application already follows P.L.2025, c.19: it adds the secondary power label and does not list a fire extinguisher. The middle fee tier says FEWER THAN TEN (10) BUSINESS DAYS, so $70.00 applies from 4 to 10 business days. The amount of any re-inspection fee is not published. Fee quotes come from a fillable PDF where the fee line wraps, so some text may be split across lines.

other_items.label: Open construction and zoning permits
other_items.detail: The Construction Records Clearance review checks for open construction permits, open zoning permits, and whether COs or approvals were issued for work on the property.
